features.title: Features

items.title: AI reference breakdown
items.text: Gemini pulls out timestamped scenes, cast, extras, style and pacing — and separately assesses who the video is aimed at and what it's selling.

items.title: Relevance check
items.text: The video's audience is compared against your product's buyers: a 0–100 score, the reasoning behind it, a list of mismatches, and concrete edits for the prompt.

items.title: Library of breakdowns
items.text: Every breakdown is saved and offered to others as a ready-made scenario, matched to the product's category and audience. The same video is never broken down twice — fast and free.

items.title: Projects, products, brand
items.text: A product catalog with photos, category, comparable prices, plus a brand manifest: style, voice-over voice, recurring characters and locations — set once, used in every video.

items.title: Characters and scenes under control
items.text: Choose who stays, who's dropped, who's swapped for your own photo — and which three images the model will actually see. Everything else is described to it in words.

items.title: A prompt you can see
items.text: The text prompt is assembled automatically from the breakdown, the product and the brand, goes through moderation, and stays fully editable.

items.title: Grok or Google Veo 3.1 — pick your engine
items.text: Grok renders by default — it's cheaper and usually faster; for a more cinematic look you can switch to Google Veo 3.1 (fast Lite or full quality). The engine and quality are chosen on every generation, independent of your service plan.

items.title: Artifact check
items.text: After generation, Gemini reviews the result and proposes a fixed prompt: stray hands, garbled text, a missing product. You can also describe the problem yourself.

items.title: Browser and Telegram — one product
items.text: Works as a regular website and as a Telegram Mini App at the same time, with no difference in functionality — start in the browser, continue in Telegram.

items.title: AI sketch instead of a product photo
items.text: If there is nothing to shoot the product with, or someone else's packaging must not be shown, the service draws it as a sketch and puts it in the frame. Available on every plan — only the daily quota differs.

items.title: Greeting video
items.text: A project type of its own: occasion, recipient's name, sender's name and tone — the output is a personal greeting video, not an ad. Available on every plan; the plan only affects quality and delivery.

items.title: Tutorial from a client's website
items.text: A step-by-step wizard drives a browser through your client's website and builds a tutorial video out of it — up to a live sign-in to a personal account when a step needs authorisation. Standard and above.

items.title: Your own voice: clone, dub, provider
items.text: The voice is cloned from your recording, and the voice-over either sits on top of Veo's audio or replaces it entirely as a dub. The synthesis provider is chosen explicitly — ElevenLabs or Resemble — and previewed before you pay.

items.title: Feed, likes and reposts
items.text: Approved videos land in the product's shared feed: likes, reposts and a public page per video with a “make one like this” button. Publishing is Standard and above.

marketplace.title: Marketplace and auctions
marketplace.lead: A second venue runs alongside the generator: a directory of real creators and open bidding on finished videos. Separate address, the same Telegram login.

items.title: Creator directory
items.text: A catalog of creators and agencies with portfolios of real work, niches and a price range. No tender and no prepayment on the platform — you get in touch and agree directly.

items.title: Brief with matching
items.text: Describe the product and the task — the venue picks matching creators from the catalog and separately advises which format and render quality suit the platform you publish on.

items.title: Auction of finished videos
items.text: Creators put finished videos up for open bidding: starting price, bids, “buy now”, exclusive lots and flash prices. A lot is protected against a last-second bid.

items.title: Brand book and collections
items.text: A five-step brand-book wizard — name, style, voice, characters, locations — attaches to the brief so the creator sees your visual identity right away. Work is grouped into themed collections by tag.

marketplace.liveNote: Some flash lots get a live broadcast with an AI host — only if the seller has explicitly agreed to stream their lot.

steps.title: Four steps
steps.lead: From the occasion to a finished file.

items.title: Describe the occasion
items.text: Occasion, recipient's name, who it is from, and the tone. You can write your own text right away — then the AI leaves it alone.

items.title: Add photos
items.text: Up to seven images — the recipient, a place, anything. This step is optional: the video works without them too.

items.title: Check the script
items.text: The service writes a short text for the occasion and tone. You see all of it and can edit it before rendering.

items.title: Get the video
items.text: Download the finished video, send it as a link, or publish it as its own page.

price.title: What it costs
price.text: Nothing right now: all three plans are free and switch inside the app. The plan decides the resolution — 480p, 720p or 1080p.

items.question: How long does a video take?
items.answer: Usually a few minutes. The exact time depends on current load — you can close the page while it renders and come back later.

items.question: What language will the greeting be in?
items.answer: The service writes the text in Russian. The interface is available in five languages, but the greeting script itself is currently generated in Russian only — if you need another language, type your own text at the script step and it goes into the video as is.

items.question: What happens to the photos and the recipient's name?
items.answer: They are used for your video only. The recipient's name never lands in a public title on its own: if you publish the video as a page, the title carries the occasion, and the name only if you put it there yourself. Details are in the terms of use.

items.question: Can I keep it a surprise?
items.answer: Yes. The result is an ordinary file and an ordinary link — when and how to send it is up to you. Scheduled “unlocks on the day” delivery does not exist yet.

items.question: What if I don't like the result?
items.answer: You can edit the script before rendering and render the video again. All plans are free right now, so re-rendering costs nothing.

items.question: Can I record something other than a greeting?
items.answer: Yes. Besides holidays there is an apology, words of support for someone who is ill, and a condolence. For those the service writes differently, does not congratulate, and does not offer a playful tone.

details.title: More about the project
details.lead: How the thing behind the buttons actually works — no marketing promises.

items.title: What a "breakdown" actually is, and why it's this detailed
items.text: The reference goes into Gemini whole — as a YouTube link or a file. What comes back is a structure: timestamped scenes with headings, cast members with a description of their look and role, extras kept separate from the cast, visual style, pacing, aspect ratio, plus an assessment of the video's audience and what it's selling. A breakdown isn't a summary — it's the raw material the prompt is later built from: every piece of it can be dropped, edited or replaced.

items.title: Why relevance is scored separately
items.text: A winning video isn't universal — it worked for its own audience. A separate check compares who the reference is aimed at with who buys your product — by age, gender, interests, category and price tier — and answers with a 0–100 score, the reasoning behind it, a list of mismatches, and concrete prompt edits. Sometimes the honest answer is: pick a different reference.

items.title: The brand manifest — set once, used in every video
items.text: Style, tone, voice-over voice, recurring characters and locations are described once and plugged into every video of the brand. A session gets a copy of the manifest at launch time: edits inside a video don't change the brand itself, and changing the brand doesn't retroactively rewrite what's already been made.

items.title: What the model sees as an image, and what as words
items.text: The service limits the set of images sent to the generation model (Grok or Google Veo) to three reference images. It shows exactly which three will be sent — characters, your scenes, brand scenes, product photo — and lets you assemble that set by hand. Anything that doesn't make the slots is described in the prompt as text instead of being lost.

items.title: The library of breakdowns and privacy
items.text: The breakdown of every public video is saved and offered to others as a ready-made scenario — making a repeat analysis unnecessary. Breakdowns of videos uploaded as a file are private: only the author sees them, and they never appear in shared results. Under the terms of use, breakdowns themselves are the service's intellectual property; your product, your materials and the finished video remain yours.

items.title: Files and how long they're kept
items.text: References, product photos, frame captures and finished videos live in Vercel Blob. Every file has an owner in the database, and deleting the owner deletes the file: an expired session takes its files with it, a deleted product takes its photo, a deleted manifest takes its character and scene photos. Daily cleanup is backed up by a separate sweep for orphaned files.

items.title: Browser and Telegram — one app
items.text: The same product opens as a regular website and as a Telegram Mini App, with no difference in capabilities. An anonymous session works without signing in; signing in through Telegram is needed for projects, the product catalog, the brand manifest and any plan above Lite — those are tied to a user.

items.title: Open source
items.text: The source code is available on GitHub; development followed the GitHub Spec Kit methodology — the spec and implementation plan live in the repository next to the code and are updated along with it.

items.question: Do I need to sign up?
items.answer: No. The session is anonymous and created automatically on your first visit — you only need to accept the public offer and terms of use once, before your first breakdown. Signing in through Telegram is available but optional: it's needed for projects, the product catalog, the brand manifest, and to come back to your sessions later.

items.question: Which video formats are supported?
items.answer: MP4, MOV and AVI up to 100MB, or simply a link to a public YouTube video — in which case there's nothing to download or upload at all.

items.question: How long does video generation take?
items.answer: Once the prompt is approved, the video is usually ready in 3–5 minutes — the exact time depends on the chosen generation engine (Grok by default, Google Veo 3.1 with Fast/Standard modes is also available) and current load.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: Right now, nothing: all three plans — Lite, Standard and Premium — are free and switch right inside the app. This is a rollout period; whatever you've already made stays yours once paid plans arrive. Later, Lite is planned to become conditionally free — in exchange for liking the project's YouTube channel and sending a few links to the service.

items.question: What's the difference between the plans?
items.answer: Lite is the minimal path: a reference breakdown and a 16:9 or 9:16 video; the greeting video and the AI product sketch are available on any plan. Standard adds the relevance check, the video audit, the brand manifest, your own scenes, photo character swaps, any aspect ratio, voice cloning, the tutorial from a client's website, publishing and the feed. Premium is Standard plus the library of ready-made breakdowns and dubbing: Veo's audio is replaced by your voice entirely. The plan can be changed at any time and does not touch projects, videos or breakdowns you have already made.

items.question: Where are my files stored, and when are they deleted?
items.answer: In Vercel Blob — the reference, product photos and the finished video all live in the same storage. Every file has an owner in the database: an expired session takes its files with it, a deleted product takes its photo, a deleted manifest takes its character and scene photos. Cleanup runs daily, and a separate pass picks up orphaned files.

items.question: Who owns the breakdowns and the finished videos?
items.answer: The service creates the reference breakdown, and under the terms of use the breakdowns belong to it — that's exactly what lets the library offer them to other users. Your product, your uploaded materials and the generated video remain yours. Breakdowns of videos uploaded as a file are private: only the author sees them.

items.question: Can I use it from Telegram?
items.answer: Yes — the same product works both as a regular website in a browser and as a Telegram Mini App inside Telegram, with the same set of features.

items.question: Can I manually edit the video breakdown or the prompt?
items.answer: Yes, at both steps: after the automatic reference analysis and after the automatic prompt generation, both results can be edited before moving on.

items.question: Is this an open-source project?
items.answer: Yes — the source code is available on GitHub, and development followed the GitHub Spec Kit methodology.

items.question: What is the marketplace and how is it different from the generator?
items.answer: It is a second venue alongside the generator, at its own address and with the same Telegram login. In the generator the AI makes the video from your reference; on the marketplace a real creator makes it — you find them in the catalog by portfolio and niche, or post a brief and the venue picks matching ones. You get in touch and settle up directly: there is no tender and no prepayment through the platform right now.

items.question: How does the video auction work?
items.answer: A creator puts an already finished video up as a lot: a starting price, open bids and, if they chose so, a “buy now” button. There are exclusive lots and flash prices. A last-second bid cannot snatch a lot — the time is extended automatically. Some flash lots have a live broadcast with an AI host, and only with the seller's explicit consent.

items.question: Can I make something other than an ad?
items.answer: Yes, there are two more project types. A greeting video: occasion, recipient's name, sender's name and tone — the output is a personal video, available on any plan. A tutorial from a client's website: the wizard drives a browser through the site and builds a tutorial video out of what happened on screen, up to a live sign-in to a personal account — Standard and above.
